text.tspan: Japan is an island nation in East Asia, located in the
northwest Pacific Ocean. It comprises four main islands—
Honshu, Hokkaido, Kyushu, and Shikoku—along with
• World's 4th largest economy by nominal GDP
• Known for technology, cuisine, and traditional culture

g.text: Japan boasts a rich cultural heritage spanning millennia, blending ancient traditions with cutting-edge modernity. From the serene temples of Kyoto to the neon-lit streets of Tokyo, it offers a unique juxtaposition of old and new. The country is globally renowned for its contributions to technology, automotive manufacturing, anime, manga, and cuisine.

As a developed nation, Japan faces demographic challenges including an aging population and low birth rates, which shape its economic and social policies. The nation maintains one of the world's highest life expectancies and standards of living.
GDP declined from $4.44T to $4.03T, with a peak of $5.12T in 2019. Recent decreases partly reflect currency depreciation.
The best time to visit Japan is during spring (March–May) for cherry blossoms, or autumn (September–November) for colorful foliage and pleasant weather.
Consider purchasing a Japan Rail Pass for unlimited travel on JR trains, including the famous Shinkansen bullet trains.

text.tspan: GDP Data: World Bank, Cabinet Office of Japan. Values in current US dollars.
Demographics: Statistics Bureau of Japan, Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications.
Map: Simplified representation; city coordinates are approximate.
Note: Japan's nominal GDP peaked at $5.12 trillion in 2019.
